📌 Private Order Flow: Hiding a Trade Before Execution

Main Points
⏺ In a public mempool, other participants can see your transaction before confirmation
⏺ Private routing can hide an order from some bots and front-running strategies
⏺ This post explains why execution privacy matters for larger trades

1️⃣ Core Idea — a transaction is sent through a private channel or specialized executor instead of the public flow.
2️⃣ Why It Matters — it becomes harder for others to see your order early and jump ahead.
3️⃣ Where It Helps — large swaps, arbitrage, DeFi trades, and situations where price can worsen because of other actors.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — you now depend on a new execution route and its rules.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — understand who receives your transaction, how it is executed, and what guarantees the service provides.

Final Thoughts

Private order flow does not make execution perfect, but it can reduce the damage from public visibility. In crypto, it matters not only what you trade, but who sees it before it lands.

📌 How will ESMA supervise crypto firms under MiCA in 2027? 

📣 The European Securities and Markets Authority has set operational resilience, outsourcing and sufficient EU based operations among its main crypto supervisory priorities for 2027 as the bloc moves further into enforcement of the Markets in Crypto Assets Regulation. 

🌐 ESMA said in its 2027 work program published Monday that its work on MiCA will concentrate on coordinating national regulators and developing more consistent supervision of crypto asset service providers across the European Union. The program comes as the regulator moves from writing and implementing MiCA rules toward overseeing how licensed firms comply with them in practice.  Chair Verena Ross described the change during a meeting of the European Parliament’s Committee on Economic and Monetary Affairs, saying ESMA’s MiCA work had moved “from rulemaking towards supervision and convergence.” 

⭐️ Operational resilience will be one of the main areas under scrutiny as ESMA works with national competent authorities responsible for supervising CASPs. Outsourcing risks, liquidity, reverse solicitation and the classification of crypto assets are among the other areas identified for coordinated work in 2027. Supervisors will pay attention to whether firms maintain sufficient operations within the EU instead of relying heavily on functions or infrastructure based elsewhere.

📣 Japan arrests two suspect over 81M yen crypto police scam 

🔖 Japanese police have arrested two people suspected of helping a fake police fraud group steal cryptocurrency worth approximately 81 million yen from a woman in her 40s. The victim was allegedly told that her bank card had been connected to a large money laundering investigation. According to police information cited by FNN, the group claimed a fraud case had caused 600 billion yen in losses and that around 400 accounts had been used to launder funds.

⚠️ FNN reported that the caller told the woman her card appeared among accounts connected with the supposed money laundering investigation. The caller then claimed she was close to being arrested and needed to “prove her innocence.” Police allege that the false accusation eventually led the victim to transfer cryptocurrency worth around 81 million yen. The assets were valued at approximately $515,000 using the conversion cited in reports on the case.

‼️ Investigators have not publicly identified the cryptocurrencies involved or disclosed the wallet addresses that received the assets. Available reporting therefore does not establish how the cryptocurrency was subsequently moved, converted or withdrawn. The Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department believes Okayama and Minamisawa participated in a larger organization. Known losses from fraud cases involving the two suspects have reached approximately 240 million yen, according to FNN.
